_: Live works chosen for the Dutch Golden Age collection page, decided by a subagent on art-historical grounds, delegated by Charlie on 2026-09-23.
criteria: Paintings by painters trained in the Dutch Republic, made c. 1588 to 1700 (the core period ends in 1672; works by painters whose careers were already under way by then are kept up to 1700). Works made abroad by such painters, and period workshop replicas, count; 18th-century work does not.

why.vl-0086: Jan Wijnants, c. 1660 to 1680: Haarlem-born dune landscape painter working in Amsterdam.
why.vl-0038: Jacob van Ruisdael, c. 1670: the leading Dutch landscape painter of the period.
why.vl-0485: Anonymous, after Willem Kalf, 1665 to 1670: the National Gallery of Art calls it a workshop replica from Kalf's Amsterdam years, so a Dutch painting of the period.
why.vl-0445: Willem Kalf, 1663: Amsterdam pronk still life at its height.
why.vl-0349: Emanuel de Witte, 1669: Amsterdam church interior, a Dutch specialty genre.
why.vl-0037: Abraham van Beyeren, c. 1660 to 1666: banquet still life, The Hague and Delft circle.
why.vl-0176: Otto Marseus van Schrieck, before 1678: inventor of the forest-floor still life, active in Amsterdam from 1657.
why.vl-0454: Willem Kalf, undated (active 1640s to 1680s): signed nautilus-cup still life of his Amsterdam type.
why.vl-0420: Willem Kalf, c. 1655 to 1660: Amsterdam period, Rijksmuseum.
why.vl-0421: Willem Kalf, c. 1653: the drinking-horn still life, National Gallery London.
why.vl-0437: Willem van Aelst, 1657: Delft-born; the year he returned from Florence to Amsterdam.
why.vl-0423: Willem Kalf, 1678: after 1672, but by a painter active in the Republic since the 1640s, still within c. 1700.
why.vl-0177: Pieter de Ring, before 1660: Leiden pupil of Jan Davidsz. de Heem.
why.vl-0385: Otto Marseus van Schrieck, undated (died 1678): forest-floor still life, his own genre.
why.vl-0439: Willem Kalf, 1635 to 1646 per Commons: most likely his Paris years (1642 to 1646); a Rotterdam-born painter working abroad is still Dutch school.
why.vl-0447: Willem Kalf, 1643 per Commons: painted in Paris; early pronk still life by a Dutch painter, counted as Dutch school like Italianates working in Rome.

borderline_excluded.vl-0087: Adriaen Coorte, 1701: dated after even the stretched end of the period, and his whole career (c. 1683 to 1707) comes after 1672. Many surveys still end the Golden Age with him, so this is the easiest call to reverse.
borderline_excluded.vl-0178: Jan van Huysum, 1700 to 1749: an 18th-century painter (born 1682); his bright decorative florals are the phase after the Golden Age.
borderline_excluded.vl-0252: Jan van Huysum, 1722: 18th century; same reason as vl-0178.
borderline_excluded.vl-0253: Jan van Huysum, 1720: 18th century; same reason as vl-0178.
borderline_excluded.vl-0275: Jan van Huysum, 1721: 18th century; same reason as vl-0178.
borderline_excluded.vl-0343: Jan van Huysum, 1722: 18th century; same reason as vl-0178.
borderline_excluded.vl-0380: Jan van Huysum, 1731 to 1732: 18th century; same reason as vl-0178.
borderline_excluded.vl-0032: Maria Sibylla Merian, 1705: an engraving from a printed book, not a painting; German-born and after 1700.
